Animate a Plot

Source: R/animate.R
animate.Rd

Evaluates a plot call repeatedly while one or more running parameters step through their values.

Usage

animate(expr, ..., delay = 0.2, loops = 1)

Arguments

expr

the plot call (or a {} block of several calls) containing the running parameter(s).

...

the running parameters as named vectors or lists, e.g. i = 1:20. Several parameters are stepped through in parallel and recycled to the longest one. Names must be unique, empty parameters are not allowed.

delay

time per frame in seconds, a single finite, non-negative number.

loops

number of runs, a non-negative whole number. Inf repeats until interrupted.

Value

The number of frames per run, invisibly.

Details

The plot call is captured unevaluated, so it can be handed over directly or by means of the native pipe (plot(...) |> animate(i = 1:10)). Each frame is drawn within grDevices::dev.hold() / grDevices::dev.flush() to avoid flickering. The time needed for drawing is deducted from delay, such that the frame rate stays constant as long as drawing is faster than delay.

Examples

# \donttest{
x <- cumsum(rnorm(100))
animate(plot(x[1:i], type = "l", xlim = c(1, 100), ylim = range(x)),
        i = 2:100, delay = 0.05)




































































































# two parameters running in parallel, using the pipe
curve(dnorm(x, mean = m), -6, 6, col = col, lwd = 2, ylim = c(0, 0.4)) |>
  animate(m = seq(-3, 3, 0.25), col = hcl.colors(25), delay = 0.1)

























# }
